title: Quiz 7 — Kubo magnitudes with symmetry, self-consistent anharmonic phonons

questions.question: What does symmetry alone NOT give for a response tensor?
questions.explanation: Neumann's principle fixes the shape; magnitudes need a Kubo (or Boltzmann) calculation.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many components must postw90 compute to know the full spin Hall tensor of fcc Pt?
questions.explanation: Cubic m-3m1′: σ^x_yz = σ^y_zx = σ^z_xy = −σ^x_zy = ... — one independent number.

questions.question: Which postw90 keywords select σ^z_xy (flow x, field y, spin z)?
questions.explanation: J^{S_k}_i = σ^k_ij E_j ↔ shc_alpha = i (flow), shc_beta = j (field), shc_gamma = k (spin).

questions.question: Hands-on: from the toy Pt scan, the value of σ^x_zy at E_F = 0 in (ħ/e) S/cm?
questions.explanation: σ^x_zy = −σ^x_yz = −σ^z_xy = −1985.3 by cubic symmetry.

questions.question: Hands-on: fitted anomalous Hall conductivity σ_xy of the toy bcc Fe file at E_F = 0 (S/cm)?
questions.explanation: Only h_z is allowed for m ∥ z; the fit keeps σ_xy and discards the forbidden parts.

questions.question: Hands-on: what does SymPhase report about the toy Fe data?

options.b: non-zero components that symmetry forbids (σ_yz, σ_zx) and a 0.27 % violation

questions.explanation: Forbidden non-zero components flag k-mesh convergence or frame problems in the Kubo run.

questions.question: Why compute a 'check component' in a symmetry-driven Kubo run?

options.b: an independent Kubo evaluation of a component predicted by symmetry verifies frame, spin order and convergence

questions.explanation: SymPhase picks the non-pivot component with the largest predicted value and compares.

questions.question: Hands-on: |σ_xy| of the Haldane model (t2 = 0.1, φ = π/2, M = 0) in the gap, in e²/h?
questions.explanation: Chern number ±1: quantised anomalous Hall conductance.

questions.question: Hands-on: Haldane model with M = 1.0 eV (> 3√3 t2): σ_xy in the gap is …
questions.explanation: The gap closes at M = 3√3 t2 ≈ 0.52 eV; beyond it the Chern number is 0.

questions.question: Hands-on: Kane–Mele spin Hall conductivity σ^z_xy at E_F = 0.5 eV (in the band) in (ħ/e) e²/h (3 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 0.591: outside the gap the spin Hall conductivity is no longer quantised.

questions.question: Hands-on: 3D stack of Haldane layers, c = 5 Å: σ_xy in S/cm (integer)?
questions.explanation: (e²/h)/c = 3.874×10⁻⁵ S / 5×10⁻⁸ cm = 774.8 S/cm — the unit check of the solver.

questions.question: Which contributions does the built-in intrinsic Kubo solver NOT include?

options.b: Fermi-surface (∝ 1/Γ) terms such as T-odd spin conductivities, and r.dat position terms

questions.explanation: It is the Fermi-sea (Berry-type) formula in the tight-binding convention.

questions.question: In TDEP, what must be added to the phonon free energy F_ph of outfile.free_energy?

options.b: the renormalised baseline U0 (second value of outfile.U0)

questions.explanation: F = F_ph[ω_eff] + U0; the further values of outfile.U0 are higher-order corrections.

questions.question: Why does SymPhase require e_static when the TDEP baseline (or an SSCHA total free energy) is used?

options.b: U0 and SSCHA totals contain the static lattice energy; only F − E_static may be added to the DFT energy of a hull entry

questions.explanation: Otherwise the static energy would be counted twice.

questions.question: The SCHA free energy compared with the exact one is …

options.b: always higher or equal (Gibbs–Bogoliubov variational bound)

questions.explanation: A variational (Gaussian) trial density matrix gives an upper bound to F.

questions.question: Hands-on: quartic oscillator (k = 2000, λ = 1200, Fe mass) at 1000 K: harmonic error F_harm − F_exact in meV (1 decimal)?
questions.explanation: −5.07 meV, versus +0.22 meV for SCHA.

questions.question: With a positive quartic term, how do SCHA phonon frequencies change on heating?
questions.explanation: Larger fluctuations at high T probe the stiffer x⁴ part of the potential.

questions.question: Hands-on: stabilisation temperature of Ni3Al-D019 in the SCHA hull (NiAl_scph.csv) in K?
questions.explanation: ≈ 790 K with anharmonic phonons.

questions.question: Hands-on: the same transition with harmonic phonons only (same k), in K?
questions.explanation: ≈ 556 K: ignoring anharmonic hardening underestimates T* by ≈ 235 K.

questions.question: What does FreeEnergySurface do with total free energies at several volumes?

options.b: minimises F(V, T) over V at each T -> V(T), G(T), β, B_T (anharmonic QHA)

questions.explanation: It is the QHA minimisation, with anharmonic (TDEP/SSCHA) free energies instead of harmonic ones.
